problem: Visual navigation models (VNMs) need egocentric onboard cameras, compute and pre-built topological maps for long-range navigation. Remote surveillance cameras could replace these, but their oblique view leaves the robot's local surroundings occluded, and no diverse remote-viewpoint training data exists.
motivation: Surveillance cameras are already widely deployed, always up to date, and attached to network compute. Using one as both observation source and implicit map would allow low-cost robots without onboard vision or maps. The key observation is that the exocentric view lacks local geometry near the robot, so an egocentric depth can be synthesized from it, and training can rely entirely on procedurally generated simulation data.
key_idea: Train a policy in randomized synthetic worlds that predicts robot-centric waypoints from remote-camera depth, augmented by a diffusion-based exo2ego module that hallucinates the robot's egocentric depth, plus DAgger-style recovery data.
insight: The synthesized egocentric depth helps mainly when large obstacles occlude the space ahead of the robot: removing exo2ego drops Warehouse SR from 70% to 26% and real Wall SR from 100% to 40%. In open scenes (Random Pillar, real Forest) it gives no gain or a slight loss (88 vs 91; 76 vs 92). DAgger-style recovery data matters a lot, e.g. Warehouse SR 43% to 70% and Book Store w/o exo2ego 44% to 84%, because expert demonstrations never visit near-collision states.
method: Problem setup: a fixed uncalibrated remote camera gives observations; the policy outputs H future robot-centric metric waypoints toward a pixel goal. It runs on the camera-side compute, and the robot needs only a 2D LiDAR and a local controller.

Observation model: the last N=5 normalized exocentric depth frames (from monocular depth estimation of the remote RGB), the robot's normalized pixel location, its relative orientation, and the synthesized ego depth. Depth is used to reduce appearance cues.

Navigation policy: an ACT-style CVAE transformer. Depth images are encoded by ResNet-34; pixel, orientation, goal and latent z are linear tokens; H learned queries decode a chunk of H=5 waypoints. Loss is L1 plus a KL term (beta=1); z is fixed to the prior mean at test time. 63.6M parameters.

exo2ego module: a conditional DDPM with a DiT-S/2 denoiser (32.8M parameters, x0-prediction). It generates a 32x32 ego depth from the exo depth history cropped around the robot, conditioned on robot pixel and orientation. It uses 8 DDIM steps (~30 ms) and is trained with MSE against GT ego depth, separately from the policy.

Synthetic data: Gazebo worlds built procedurally from pillar and wall primitives with random sizes, shapes, densities and layouts, plus randomized camera poses. Nav2 is the expert; about 50k episodes give about 1M 5-step samples.
DAgger-inspired recovery data: roll out the current policy, collect expert recovery trajectories from near-collision or stuck states, and retrain. About 5k recovery episodes over two loops.
Shared local control: all methods use the same LiDAR-based MPPI controller to track waypoints with reactive avoidance; global detours come only from the waypoints.

setting.backbone: ACT-style CVAE transformer policy with ResNet-34 encoders + DiT-S/2 diffusion exo2ego module (trained from scratch on synthetic data; ResNet ImageNet-pretrained)
setting.training_data: ~50k synthetic Gazebo episodes (~1M 5-step samples) from randomized pillar/wall worlds and camera poses, Nav2 expert, incl. ~5k DAgger recovery episodes; no real data
setting.observation: single fixed remote RGB camera, converted to monocular depth (5-frame history), plus robot image-space pixel position and orientation; no onboard camera
setting.action_space: predicted robot-centric metric waypoints (chunk of 5), tracked by a LiDAR-based MPPI controller
setting.privileged: robot pixel pose and orientation in the remote image: simulator ground truth in sim, AprilTag in the real world; the last observed pose is held under occlusion

results: ReVNM beats IBVS in simulation by 10/13/18 SR points (88/88/70% vs 78/75/52%) and greatly beats NoMaD (best 40% SR after fine-tuning). In the real world it gets 76% on Forest and 100% on Wall vs IBVS 12% and 0%, with no fine-tuning on a different robot.
limitations: Requires robot pose in the remote image (AprilTag in real experiments) and adequate camera coverage of the workspace; needs marker-free pose estimation and multi-camera handover.
Synthesized ego depth can be inaccurate or over-conservative (hurts in open Forest scenes, 76% vs 92%), and a gap to oracle-ego remains.
Real-world evaluation is small (two scenarios, 30 trials); the NoMaD baseline could only be run in simulation.
compares_to: IBVS (Robinson et al., SAM3 + A* + pure pursuit)
